summary: The refactoring removes the null check for `user.address` in `getUserCity`. This causes unhandled `TypeError` exceptions whenever `getUserCity` is called with a user object missing an `address` property.

findings.title: Uncaught TypeError when user object lacks address property
findings.description: Removing `if (!user.address)` check causes `getUserCity` to throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city')` if a user object does not have an `address` property or if `address` is null/undefined.
findings.verificationHypothesis: Calling getUserCity with a user object that lacks an address property (e.g., `{ name: 'Alice' }`) will throw a TypeError.

suggestedReproduction.preconditions: The input user object does not have an `address` property defined.
suggestedReproduction.expectedBehavior: The function returns `null` or `undefined` gracefully without throwing.
suggestedReproduction.suspiciousBehavior: The function throws a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city')`.
